title: The runbook Starting the autopilot lacks the prerequisites of a first unattended run and overstates what is enforced
goal: the `Starting the autopilot` section of kb/_self/backlog.md is correct for a first unattended run on this Mac: step 1 says what the rehearsal does not test (permissions, hooks, land, glab, the manager skill, the real allow rules); step 2 names the prerequisites (a clean main checkout, an integration remote that works unattended: an ssh key without a passphrase prompt and `glab auth status`, a trusted workspace with the project's MCP servers approved and the kb server Connected per `claude mcp list`, /kb-setup done) and starts the manager session with KB_NO_PUBLISH_HOOK=1 exported (never KB_HEADLESS_RUNNER); step 4 says tasks fire only when the session is idle, a permission prompt stalls the loop, and the first tick starts runners on the operator-started sprints that `autopilot.py status` lists, with how to hold one back; step 5 reads kb/_self/reports/autopilot-digest.md or runs `kbdecide.py digest` only when stopped (it rewrites a tracked file); step 6 adds that /exit ends background runner starts as error and that a SIGKILLed runner's child is ended with `backlog.py procs --end`; step 7 states which guarantees hold (the headless env refusals) and which depend on items not landed yet; found by the SP-itmjxudu review

run: import sys,pathlib,re;t=pathlib.Path("kb/_self/backlog.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8");i=t.index("Starting the autopilot");s=t[i:i+9000];need=["KB_NO_PUBLISH_HOOK","glab auth status","claude mcp list","does not test","hold"];miss=[n for n in need if n not in s];print(miss);sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)

repro_reason: the defect is the wording of a runbook a person follows; the repro reads the section for the phrases the first run needs
